title: Limited Drop Alert Video Template | AIVideosUGC
description: Make a short alert video for a small release or restock from one product photo. After you download it, add the date, the quantity, and your link.
h1: Limited Drop Alert Video for a Restock or Small Release
lead: A limited drop alert video is a short clip for a small release or restock. Put the product in a scene. Add a voiceover, a spoken voice, and captions, words on the screen. Add the date only after you download. Credits, what each job spends, are shown before you start.
steps_h2: Make a Limited Release Ad in 3 Steps
steps_lead: The scene shows the product. Add the spoken line here, and keep the date and quantity editable after download.

steps.d: Upload one clear photo of the item in this release, or paste its product page link.
Name how the product appears and a short spoken line, then pick a size and a length from 6 to 30 seconds.
Download the alert, add the date and quantity, and post to TikTok, Facebook, or Instagram. Pause it when you sell out.

faq.q: What is a limited drop alert video?
faq.a: A ready scene for a short release. You add your product photo, a hook (the opening line), a script (the words), and a voiceover (a spoken voice). An AI actor, a generated person, can hold the item. You type the date and the quantity after download.

faq.q: How do I build the alert?
faq.a: Upload the photo or paste a product page link. Take the script, pick an AI actor and a spoken voice, choose a size and a length, then download. You can make several versions from that same photo.

faq.q: Why start from a product photo instead of filming the drop?
faq.a: The scene comes from the photo or the product link. You can prepare the alert before the release, and you do not need a creator for every color.

faq.q: Who is this release alert for?
faq.a: Shops with a short time to sell, including shoes, clothes, a beauty color, or a home restock. They post on TikTok, Instagram Reels, or a product page.

faq.q: Can a first-time seller use it?
faq.a: Yes. One clear photo and a short line are enough. You can set words on screen, music, and the spoken line before you download.

faq.q: Can the clip show a live countdown or the stock count?
faq.a: Add the countdown, the date, and the quantity as text after download. This tool does not read a clock or a stock number from your store.

faq.q: Which size and length fit a drop post?
faq.a: Use 9:16, a tall phone shape, for TikTok and Instagram Reels. 1:1 is a square for the main feed. You can also pick 16:9 (wide), 4:3, or 3:4 (tall). Lengths are 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds. You can post to TikTok or Meta (Facebook and Instagram).

faq.q: Does it include music, captions, or a voiceover?
faq.a: Yes. In the editor, set a spoken voice, words on screen, and a track from the music library. You can speak the line again in another language.

A video spends 24 credits for 6 seconds, 40 for 10, 60 for 15, and 120 for 30. Credits are what the job spends. You see the cost first, and a failed job returns those credits. Plans start at $24.50 a month. There is no free plan. The download has no watermark, nothing stamped on the file.

faq.q: What should I do when the drop sells out?
faq.a: Pause or replace the ad and change the quantity line. The API lets your product list start the next alert. Any person on screen is an AI actor, a generated person, not a buyer.

steps.sourceHint: Show the full shoe shape and color in a clear view.
steps.prompt: An adult hiker ties the coral trail shoes on a rocky trail, then stands so the sole and both shoes stay visible. Leave room above the shoes for a date you add after download.

reviews.h2: How Shops Make a Release Alert
reviews.lead: Examples of how a shop makes a short release alert. You still add the date and the quantity after download.

items.t: A finished alert from one product photo
items.d: Example: a watch shop uploads a photo of the watch and gets a short alert it can post. The release date is typed on later.

items.t: The still and the clip in one project
items.d: Example: an apparel shop builds the jacket photo and the restock alert together, in one project, without a second app.

items.t: Hold the pair, or start from the link
items.d: Example: a shoe shop pastes the product page link, or uploads the pair, and the clip shows those shoes held up for the release.

items.t: An AI actor, then captions in the editor
items.d: Example: the shop picks an AI actor, a generated person, to hold the jacket. It trims the clip in the editor and adds words on screen.

items.t: The same drop in another language
items.d: Example: a beauty shop keeps one color reveal and speaks the line again in a second language for the other market.

items.t: A track and a spoken line before download
items.d: Example: a home shop adds a spoken voice and a music track, then edits both before the candle restock goes out.

items.t: An AI actor for a small release
items.d: Example: a bag shop uses an AI actor, a generated person, to show a small release. Someone new to video can start from one photo.

items.t: Same generated person, no new lights
items.d: Example: a drink shop uses a digital twin, the same generated person, for each new can. The team does not set up lights again.

items.t: A script, a voice, and a second version
items.d: Example: a jewelry shop pastes the product link, takes the words and the spoken voice, then makes a second version from the same photo.

items.t: Post to TikTok or Meta, or use the API
items.d: Example: a fitness shop posts the gear alert to TikTok or Meta (Facebook and Instagram). The API lets the store's product list start the next alert.
